key_insight: The paper shows how to spend a limited annotation budget optimally over time to reduce variance in off-policy evaluation when rewards are costly or missing.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical way to obtain trustworthy policy-value estimates from sequential, partially labeled data such as clinical notes, safety reviews, or human preference records.
method: Use doubly robust off-policy evaluation with missing rewards.
Derive variance-optimal annotation probabilities for sequential forward-monotone protocols.
Implement a feasible batch-adaptive annotation strategy under a fixed labeling budget.
evidence_signal: Across simulations and two real datasets, the method reduced RMSE by 34–65% on the homelessness casenote task and 17–68% on the housing-application progress task at 40% annotation budget and above, and by 55–62% on LMArena across all budgets.
watch_item: The approach depends on a sequential annotation design and accurate implementation of the batch-adaptive policy, so gains may weaken if annotation decisions or missingness assumptions are poorly matched to the data.
paper_title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation
